# clause, so `sink(count = 1)` in the default calls the outer method and the
# assignment writes `count` (binding line 4, writes lines 5 and 35, span 30).

# ctor-clause-scope.scala: the constructor parameter is in scope only in
# later clauses. Early (clause 1) shadows the outer method, so the call
# through it records no write. Same (own clause) and Late (later clause)
# do not shadow, so `sink(count = 1)` resolves to the outer method, which
# lacks `count`, and the assignment writes `count` (bindings 54 and 94).
# The calls sit in a nested helper: a constructor default is not function
# scope, so a bare block there binds nothing observable.
src/ctor-clause-scope.scala:54 info complexity/mutable-span
src/ctor-clause-scope.scala:94 info complexity/mutable-span
